note: The regression trip-wire for the usefulness gate: twelve cases that need no
deliberation. A thin v1 prompt is expected to pass the six keeps and fail
several of the rejects; that is the baseline, not a defect.
Capability cases are added from observed failures, not enumerated here. The
first three to expect are afterimage (transparent compound, concept worth
naming), doggedness (redundant with dogged, see #59) and draconian (OEWN
Endorsement counts are deliberately absent from this file. Endorsement must
not reach the prompt, and these twelve must be excluded from the retention
audit sample, which requires words no golden case has touched.

cases.why: High-utility cross-domain adjective. If the gate rejects this, the gate is broken.
Precise negative adjective with no everyday substitute; carries a sense harmful does not.
Verb, for part-of-speech spread. The tier-2 band skews adjectival and the set should not.
Noun, for part-of-speech spread. Common in professional writing.
Derived from Laconia but OEWN carries only the general sense. Deliberate contrast with draconian, where the general sense is missing and the gate should fail for evidence reasons rather than taste.
Semantically adjacent to spartan, which survives the demonym filter on its figurative senses. Both should be servable.
Informal and dated slang. Product owner's canonical example of a word that will never belong.
Informal and derogatory; Wiktionary labels it so. Transparent, and the concept needs no new word.
A fact to look up, not vocabulary that expands expressive range. Knowing it changes no sentence the learner would write.
Zipf 5.4. Every adult learner already has it. The gate must reject on being too common, not only on being too obscure.
Botany and zoology only. Tier 3 by the Beck/McKeown split: domain-specific rather than cross-domain.
Also removed mechanically before this gate runs. Kept here as defence in depth, so a change to the pool filter cannot silently admit demonyms.
